Title: Diagnosis of test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode`
Details: The test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode` constructs a TarArchiveEntry with a non-ASCII directory name (containing umlauts) "föö/". It then creates a TarArchiveOutputStream and sets `setAddPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames(true)`. It attempts to add the entry to the archive using `putArchiveEntry`.

When `putArchiveEntry` is called, the method checks if the name length exceeds the limit and whether to add PAX headers for non-ASCII names. If `addPaxHeadersForNonAsciiNames` is true and the name contains non-ASCII characters (determined via `ASCII.canEncode`), a "path" PAX header is added.

The entry's header is written via `writeEntryHeader`, which calls `TarUtils.formatNameBytes` to encode the entry name into bytes using the configured encoding.

The bug likely resides in handling the non-ASCII directory name encoding or the addition of PAX headers. Specifically, `TarUtils.formatNameBytes` attempts to encode the name into the limited space (typically 100 bytes) available for the name field in the tar header. If the encoded name size exceeds this limit, it truncates by successively shortening the name substring until it fits. This truncation might cause loss of non-ASCII characters or incorrect representation, especially impacting directory names which must end with '/'.

The test might be failing because either the non-ASCII characters in the directory name are not properly preserved due to this truncation or because the PAX headers are not correctly written or handled in POSIX mode which supports long names.

The flow of possible fault:
- The name is set with non-ASCII chars.
- POSIX mode is set for long filenames.
- `putArchiveEntry` adds PAX headers for non-ASCII names.
- The entry header is written, using the method that truncates encoded names that don't fit.
- The truncation or encoding error causes the written directory name to be incorrect or invalid, leading to test failure.

Likely fixes involve the handling of non-ASCII names in `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry` or the encoding/truncation logic in `TarUtils.formatNameBytes`.

Recommended methods to check and possibly fix:
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveEntry)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.formatNameBytes(java.lang.String, byte[], int, int, org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipEncoding)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
